title: Order of persons; generation; transition — Cap. 21 COMPLETE
pass_a_gloss: Pass A clause gloss (reordered): CHAPTER TWENTY-TWO, On GOD THE FATHER, follows. but it ought to be demonstrated out from Scripture alone. The Trinity belonging toward persons can in some way be illustrated by means belonging toward likenesses out from ye book belonging toward nature; Hence ye begetting plus begotten person constitute opposite relations. the principle by means belonging toward that same which generation comes about stands as nature. the principle that same which begets stands as ye Father; We rightly assert that same ye Father has begotten ye Son out from Himself: generation properly so called comes about by means belonging toward communication belonging toward ye whole essence. Active generation stands as attributed to ye Father; John 5:26-27. In ye order belonging toward persons we set ye begetter before ye begotten in thought — Matthew 28:19;
pass_b_english: In the order of persons we set the begetter before the begotten in thought — Matthew 28:19; John 5:26-27. Active generation is attributed to the Father; generation properly so called comes about by communication of the whole essence.

We rightly assert that the Father has begotten the Son from Himself: the principle which begets is the Father; the principle by which generation comes about is nature. Hence the begetting and begotten person constitute opposite relations.
The Trinity of persons can in some way be illustrated by likenesses from the book of nature; but it ought to be demonstrated from Scripture alone. CHAPTER TWENTY-TWO, On GOD THE FATHER, follows.
source_text: In ordine personarum generantem generato cogitando praeponimus — Matth. XXVIII.19; Joh. V.26-27. Generatio activa tribuitur Patri; generatio proprie dicta fit per communicationem totius essentiae. Recte asserimus Patrem ex se Filium genuisse: principium quod generat, Pater est; principium quo generatio fit, natura est. Hinc persona gignens et genita relationes oppositas constituunt. Trinitas personarum illustrari quodammodo potest similitudinibus e libro naturae; demonstrari autem debet e sola Scriptura. CAPUT VIGESIMUM SECUNDUM, De DEO PATRE, sequitur.
